references.title: The Best Humidifiers | Lab Tested & Ranked
Levoit OasisMist 1000S Smart Tower Humidifier Review

en.commentary: I put the Levoit LV600S first and I stand behind it. It gives me warm and cool mist in one 6L body, covers up to 753 sq ft, runs about 50 hours on low and costs around $110. That mix of output, app control and price beats everything else I can name for a bedroom or living room. The Honeywell HCM350B takes second because its UV light and wicking filter deliver clean moisture with zero white dust on the furniture, which makes it my pick for a baby room. The OasisMist 1000S gets my nod for large rooms, with a 10L tank that lasts up to 100 hours. The Classic 300S at about $72 is the value anchor, and its top-fill tank turns weekly cleaning into a two-minute job. The Dreo HM524S at 28 dB on low is a superb sleeper, though I would trust a separate hygrometer over its built-in reading. For a whole home, the AIRCARE MA1201 covers up to 3,600 sq ft and the Vornado Evap40 handles 1,000 sq ft with a five-year warranty. Pick by room size first, then by how much cleaning you will realistically do.

highlights.title: Levoit LV600S is the best all-round humidifier
highlights.body: One 6L tank gives warm mist for cold nights and cool mist for summer, and coverage reaches 753 sq ft. Around 50 hours on low means one refill lasts a work week, and the app lets me hold a target humidity without walking over to the unit.

highlights.title: Honeywell HCM350B is the baby room choice
highlights.body: The evaporative wick lets water evaporate into the room, so mineral dust stays in the filter. A UV lamp treats up to 99.9% of bacteria in the tank water. Cool mist keeps the surface free of hot water, which suits a nursery.

highlights.title: OasisMist 1000S is the large room answer
highlights.body: Its 10L tank lasts up to 100 hours and serves rooms of 300 to 600 sq ft. At about $150 it costs more than the LV600S, and it earns that price in living rooms and open-plan studios where a 6L unit runs dry too fast.

highlights.title: Classic 300S makes cleaning easy
highlights.body: The top-fill design lets me pour water straight in and lift out the tank for a quick rinse. Around $72 for 60 hours of runtime and app control makes it the humidifier I recommend to first-time buyers.

highlights.title: AIRCARE MA1201 and Vornado Evap40 cover the whole home
highlights.body: The MA1201 handles up to 3,600 sq ft with a 3.6-gallon tank and casters. The Evap40 covers 1,000 sq ft with a dual tank, a built-in humidistat and a five-year warranty. Both use wick filters, so plan on replacing them each season.

references.title: The Best Evaporative Humidifiers of 2026, Tested by Bob Vila

en.commentary:
The Levoit LV600S stays first, and this week's reading gave me a good reason to talk about the whole-house tier that sits above my bedroom picks. Bob Vila's team tested seven evaporative models over three months of fall and winter weather, and its favorite was the Levoit Superior 6000S, praised for long runtime, wide coverage, smart features and easy maintenance. Coverage of up to 3,000 square feet and a 6 gallon tank make it a serious answer for an open-plan home.

For a single room, my ranking logic holds up. The LV600S gives me warm and cool mist in one 6L body, covers a large bedroom or living room, and runs for about two days on a fill. The Honeywell HCM350B keeps second place because its filter-free design and simple controls suit people who want a dependable appliance with minimal setup. The Levoit Classic 300S remains the value pick I recommend to first-time buyers, with app control and sleep-mode noise around 28 dB.

My practical advice for the heating season is to buy a hygrometer alongside any humidifier. Comfort sits in the 40 to 50 percent range, and a cheap sensor tells you when to turn the output down before windows fog and surfaces get damp. Clean the tank on a weekly schedule, since a smart app can remind you but cannot scrub for you. Buy in the early fall while stock is plentiful, and pick the unit that matches your room size. A humidifier sized to the space runs quietly on low and does its job all night.

references.title: The Best Evaporative Humidifiers of 2026, Tested

en.commentary:
The Levoit LV600S stays first, and today I want to dig into the safety and cleaning trade-off between the top two, since it explains more about how humidifiers actually behave in a bedroom than any spec sheet number alone. The Honeywell HCM350B holds a 9.8 for safety, the highest in the whole table, because its evaporative wick design has no heating element and cannot scald a curious kid or pet, and it also cannot oversaturate a room the way a powerful ultrasonic unit can. Its 9.4 for cleaning comes from the same wick technology, since there is no water reservoir sitting in a warm mist chamber growing anything unpleasant between fills.

The LV600S answers with a 9.6 for output and a 9.6 for smart controls, the two numbers that keep it first overall. Warm and cool mist in one body covers a genuinely large room, and app control means you can dial humidity down from another floor the moment a hygrometer reading climbs too high. RTINGS' latest testing round continues to list both machines among the category's top picks for exactly these reasons, one for raw coverage and control, one for safety and simple upkeep.

My honest advice is to match the mechanism to the room. A nursery or a room with pets and curious hands is safer with the Honeywell's wick system. A large bedroom or living room where you want app control and strong output is better served by the LV600S. Either way, empty and rinse the tank on a weekly schedule, since a smart app can remind you to clean but it cannot do the scrubbing.

highlights.body: A 9.6 for output and 9.6 for smart controls let you manage humidity remotely and cover a genuinely large room.

en.commentary:
The Levoit LV600S stays first this week, and I want to shift focus to third and fourth place, two Levoit models that get overshadowed by their own sibling at the top of this table. The OasisMist 1000S holds third with a 9.4 for smart controls and a 9.4 for output, essentially matching the flagship's core numbers in a tower form factor that takes up less floor space in a smaller bedroom. Its 8.0 for value is the real gap between it and the LV600S, since the smart tower design costs more to manufacture than the LV600S's simpler hybrid ultrasonic body.

The Classic 300S in fourth takes the opposite trade off, a 9.4 for cleaning, the second best number in the whole table behind the Honeywell HCM350B, paired with an 8.2 for output that is genuinely lower than every humidifier ranked above it. Bob Vila's own testing of evaporative and hybrid humidifiers continues to note that wide mouth tanks and simple internal geometry, the exact design the Classic 300S uses, cut down real cleaning time more than any marketed anti microbial coating does.

RTINGS' ongoing humidifier test bench remains the source I check most often for output numbers across brands, since a manufacturer's own square footage claim rarely survives independent measurement. Nothing in this update changes where the LV600S sits relative to the pack, but the gap between the OasisMist and the LV600S is closer than the rank order alone suggests.

My advice for anyone shopping between Levoit's own lineup is simple. Buy the LV600S for the best all around number, the OasisMist if floor space is tight, and the Classic 300S if cleaning time matters more to you than raw output.

en.commentary:
The Levoit LV600S holds first place again, and this week I want to point to the evaporative and hybrid designs sitting in the middle of my table, since the months ahead are exactly when that engineering choice starts to matter. Once heating systems switch on for fall and winter, indoor air dries out fast, and a humidifier's real output number becomes the thing that decides whether a room actually feels comfortable.

Vornado's Evap40 in sixth uses a wicking filter and a fan in place of ultrasonic mist, and that design earns it a 9.0 for output and a 9.4 for safety, both strong numbers, while skipping the fine white mineral dust an ultrasonic unit can leave on nearby furniture. AIRCARE's MA1201 in seventh pushes the same evaporative approach further, a 9.8 for output, the highest raw number anywhere in this table, built for genuinely large rooms where a smart ultrasonic tower would run low on water long before the wick runs dry.

The trade off shows up in the smart score. Both units sit at 5.4 or below for smart controls, since a wicking filter has no app to talk to and no sensor beyond a basic dial, the honest cost of the mechanical simplicity that keeps them reliable. Bob Vila's own testing of evaporative and hybrid humidifiers keeps finding the same pattern, a wider wick surface moves more water into the air per hour than an equivalent ultrasonic disc, at the cost of the smart home integration a flagship model offers.

My ranking holds this week. For a large, dry room this winter where output matters more than an app, the AIRCARE MA1201 and the Vornado Evap40 do the actual job better than their rank alone suggests. For a bedroom where quiet, smart scheduling matters more, the LV600S at the top of my table stays the easier recommendation.

zh-tw.commentary:
Levoit LV600S 這次還是穩坐第一，這篇我想把焦點轉到中段那幾台蒸發式跟複合式加濕機，因為接下來這幾個月正是這種設計該發揮的時候。暖氣一開，室內濕度掉得很快，加濕機真正的出水量數字，才是決定房間舒不舒服的關鍵。

排名第六的 Vornado Evap40 用的是吸水棉芯加風扇的設計，出水量拿下 9.0 分，安全性更高達 9.4 分，而且不會像超音波機那樣，水裡的礦物質變成白色粉末飄到家具上。排名第七的 AIRCARE MA1201 把這套邏輯做得更徹底，出水量直接衝到 9.8 分，是整張表裡最高的數字，這種機型就是為大坪數房間設計的，智慧型超音波塔機水箱撐不到那個出水量，水就先見底了。

代價寫在智慧控制分數上，這兩台都在 5.4 分以下，畢竟棉芯機構沒有 App 可以連，濕度感應也只有基本旋鈕，這是機械結構簡單換來的可靠度，我覺得算是老實的交換。Bob Vila 實測蒸發式跟複合式加濕機時也一直看到同樣的結果，棉芯接觸面積大，每小時能送進空氣裡的水氣就是比同等級超音波機片多，只是少了旗艦機該有的智慧家庭整合。

我這次排名不變。今年冬天如果房間大又乾燥，出水量比 App 重要，AIRCARE MA1201 或 Vornado Evap40 實際表現比名次看起來更值得考慮。如果是重視安靜跟智慧排程的臥室，排名第一的 LV600S 還是比較好入手的選擇。
